answer: I would like to talk about someone I met only a few weeks ago but have not stopped thinking about. Recently I met someone at a friend's gathering who genuinely intrigued me, and I have been hoping to get to know her better. The gathering was a small dinner at a friend's home in Dhaka, when I was there visiting my elder sister. She works in an unusual field, environmental research, which immediately made her stand out in a room full of bankers and engineers. She studies how river erosion is affecting farming communities in the north of the country. What struck me was how [[articulate]] she was; she could explain complex ideas in a way that was easy to follow and genuinely interesting. We talked about climate change, the Jamuna swallowing land near my grandparents' village, and even her plans to do a PhD abroad. We ended up talking for over an hour, and the conversation never once felt [[tedious]]. She has clearly travelled widely and has a very [[broad-minded]] outlook, which I found refreshing. As for why I want to know her better, it is because she has a rare combination of intelligence and warmth. Too often first meetings feel superficial, but this one felt genuinely meaningful. We exchanged contacts, so I am hopeful we will meet again the next time I am in Dhaka. Honestly, it is quite unusual to feel [[an instant rapport]] with someone, and I do not want to let it fade.

followUps.q: Do you find it easy to talk to new people?
followUps.answer: It depends on the situation. At work I am comfortable because I know my role, but at social events I can be a bit hesitant at first. Once a conversation gets going, though, I usually [[warm up]] quickly.

followUps.q: How do you usually make new friends?
followUps.answer: Mostly through people I already know, like friends of friends or colleagues. I have made a few friends through work as well, since I meet so many different people at the consultancy.

note: Added where we met (a dinner in Dhaka while visiting my sister), what she researches and what we talked about (Jamuna erosion); replaced plain mark 'connection' with 'an instant rapport'.
